quote: The Initial Term ends November 14, 2026, making the deadline **August 16, 2026**. The MIPA was signed on October 5, 2026—nearly two months after that deadline. Schedule 3.12 states the Company "intends to deliver the Renewal Notice prior to Closing" (November 30, 2026), which is both after the contractual deadline and after the expiration date itself. If the Renewal Notice was not in fact delivered on or before August 16, 2026, the Distribution Agreement expires by its own terms on November 14, 2026, and cannot be renewed. ... the representation in Section 3.12(c) that the Distribution Agreement "remains in effect through November 2029" appears inaccurate as of the Signing Date if the Renewal Notice was not timely delivered, creating a potential indemnification claim under MIPA Section 8.2(a)
reason: The memo covers every element of the criterion. It ties Distribution Agreement §3.2 (notice at least 90 days before the term ends) to an August 16, 2026 deadline and says that deadline has passed. It reads Schedule 3.12's 'intends to deliver' language as showing no notice was sent. It concludes the agreement expires November 14, 2026, before the November 30 target closing, and lists a Velloran extension as a fix. It flags the MIPA §3.12(c) 'through November 2029' representation as inaccurate, exposing the Sellers to an indemnification claim. The memo hedges on whether notice was actually delivered, but this is reasonable diligence and does not change the substance.
